criterion: The tour opens on the instrument and the headline beside the instrument, so a visitor meets the moving subject before any row of navigation chrome.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the first screen of the tour is dominated by the instrument and its headline. Answer no when a feature list or a row of cards occupies the first screen ahead of the instrument.

criterion: The documentation shell reads as a dense organised manual, and the curve editor shows its result beside the control that caused the result.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the documentation reads quiet and dense and the editor puts its preview beside its plot. Answer no when either surface reads as a marketing page or hides the result away from the control.

criterion: Interface labels through the documentation shell are set in a monospace, and the curve editor draws each numeric readout as seven strokes per digit.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the module tree, the demo labels and the pager are set in a monospace and the editor readouts are drawn from segment strokes. Answer no when the interface is set in the reading face or the readouts are ordinary text.

criterion: Every headline on the tour sets at a line height tighter than its own font size, giving the opening the stacked look the design depends on.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the tour headlines stack with their lines almost touching. Answer no when the headlines sit at ordinary leading.

criterion: The curve editor signals its chosen preset through a change of asymmetric corner softening, and the footer joined field pair is softened along its outer edges alone.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the chosen preset tile softens a different corner from an idle tile and the footer field with its submit button reads as one joined control. Answer no when selection is signalled by colour alone or the footer pair reads as two separate controls.

criterion: Movement across the tour, the documentation shell and the curve editor shares one family of curves at one speed, and each component inside a documentation section takes its colour from that section's alias.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when movement across those three surfaces shares one speed and one easing character and a change of module recolours the tree entry, the demo panel and the article accents together. Answer no when components carry their own speeds or reach for a colour family of their own.

criterion: The header carries the wordmark on the left, five navigation calls, and the funding call on a filled ground at the right.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the header shows that arrangement on the tour, the documentation and the curve editor alike. Answer no when the wordmark, the five calls or the funding call sit somewhere else.

criterion: One token layer at the root supplies the ladder of spacing steps every gap in the documentation shell is drawn from.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when gaps across the shell land on a visible common ladder of steps. Answer no when spacing varies between surfaces with nothing in common.

criterion: The type ladder and the radius ladder are separate scales, and corner softening across the documentation shell and the curve editor lands on the radius ladder.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when text sizes and corner radii each come from their own consistent scale. Answer no when a radius or a size is chosen per component.

criterion: A specimen block in a documentation page breaks out of the article measure to sit edge to edge, and every element on the tour composes its movement from separately addressable transform channels.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a code block runs wider than the prose around it and scroll-driven movement on the tour leaves a hover-driven change on the same element intact. Answer no when the block sits inside the measure or one movement wipes out the other.

criterion: Body text on a documentation page meets the WCAG AA contrast bar against the page ground, and the dim steps used for the module tree have been measured against the same bar rather than assumed.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the article body and the tree rows both clear the WCAG AA contrast bar of 4.5 to 1 once measured. Answer no when either pairing sits below the bar.

criterion: Every target on the tour and in the documentation shell stays at least a comfortable fingertip across, and vertical sizing follows the dynamic viewport height so a phone browser chrome leaves the stage uncut.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when every control is comfortably tappable and the tour stage fits the visible window on a phone. Answer no when a target is smaller than a fingertip or the stage is clipped by browser chrome.

criterion: The instrument on the tour carries a warm rim light, the one warm value in an otherwise neutral scene, separating the object from the ground behind the object.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a warm edge light picks out the object's silhouette against the scene ground. Answer no when the object reads flat against the ground.

criterion: A menu, a dialog or the version list on the documentation shell arrives fading up from very slightly too small, and leaves the same way.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when those panels arrive with a small scale change alongside the fade. Answer no when they cut in, grow from nothing, or fade with the size held.

criterion: Every interactive element in the header lifts from a light neutral to a near-white when pointed at, and the funding call alone moves its ground instead of its text.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the navigation calls brighten their text and the funding call brightens its ground. Answer no when the lift varies between elements or the funding call behaves like the links around the call.

criterion: A curve handle in the editor carries the grab cursor at rest and the grabbing cursor during a drag.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the pointer shows an open hand over a handle and a closed hand during a drag. Answer no when the pointer stays an arrow or shows the same shape throughout.

criterion: The success message and the error message on the course waiting list sit in the document at rest and fade up when the moment comes.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when both message elements are already in the document and change their opacity. Answer no when either message is inserted into the document at the moment of use.

criterion: The footer carries four column headings, the maintainer attribution beneath a full-width wordmark, and an advertising attribution one step dimmer than every other link.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when all three are present in the footer with the attribution visibly quieter than the links around the attribution. Answer no when a heading, the attribution or the wordmark is missing, or the advertising credit reads at full strength.

criterion: The course waiting list opens on a two-line headline above two paragraphs of centred supporting copy.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the course page leads with that headline over the centred copy. Answer no when the page opens on the form or on a single line of prose.

criterion: Fourteen named objects serve the sixteen documentation modules, so two modules may share one object inside the instrument.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the instrument draws an object per module from a library of fourteen, with a shared object where the library runs out. Answer no when every module demands an object of its own or the library carries a different count.

criterion: Arriving at a tour stop rebinds the colour alias to that stop's module family, lights that module's arc, and swaps the object inside the ring together.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the colour, the lit arc and the object all change at one stop boundary. Answer no when any of the three lags behind the others or changes at a different point.

criterion: One controller on the tour derives the current stop, so a deep link lands on that stop with the intervening stops unplayed and a touch device lights the arc of the module in view.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a fragment address opens straight on its stop and every part of the tour agrees about which stop is current. Answer no when the tour plays through the stops on the way or the headline, the arc and the object disagree at a boundary.

criterion: The graduation marks around the instrument are transformed one by one from a shared parameter, so the rim reads as a dial turned by hand.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the marks move at different amounts across one scroll pass. Answer no when the whole ring turns as a single rigid group.

criterion: Scroll position on the tour sets the current stop and the interpolation between stops, and the pointer adds a small bounded parallax on top.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when scrolling drives the instrument continuously and moving the pointer tilts the view a little. Answer no when the instrument holds one state between stops or ignores the pointer.

criterion: Elapsed time alone gives the instrument a slow idle rotation and keeps the heart particles drifting when a visitor holds still.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the instrument keeps moving gently with the page untouched. Answer no when the instrument freezes the moment scrolling stops.

criterion: The tour prepares the next stop's object before the current one leaves the screen, holds at most two objects at a time, and pauses the scene when the tab is hidden.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when stops change with the object already there and the scene stops drawing on a hidden tab. Answer no when a stop change waits for a load or the scene keeps drawing in the background.

criterion: Demonstration panels in the documentation column butt against each other with a gap of nothing, and the chosen documentation version is remembered for a visitor across routes and sessions.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the panels sit flush and returning later restores the chosen version. Answer no when the panels are spaced apart or the version selection is forgotten between visits.

criterion: The server error page carries a retry control beneath its heading.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the error page offers a way to try again. Answer no when the page offers only prose.

criterion: One sampler in the curve editor feeds the plot, the tick strip, the preview and the generated code, so the four agree to the last decimal.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the drawn curve, the moving cell and the copied snippet describe the same curve. Answer no when the drawn curve and the snippet disagree in a late decimal.

criterion: A documentation article is readable before any demonstration has run, the curve editor shows a correct static plot before its own code runs, and every static asset is addressed by a digest of its own content.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when text arrives first on both surfaces and asset addresses change with their contents. Answer no when the article waits on a demonstration or an asset keeps its address through a change.

criterion: An oversized search index splits per module, scroll work runs from a frame loop over a cached position, and every reserved space on the tour holds still after first paint.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the index is fetched in parts where large, the tour scrolls smoothly, and the stage and panels occupy their space before filling. Answer no when the first search stalls, the scroll stutters, or the page jumps as content arrives.

criterion: The footer leaves a visible gap where an empty advertising slot sits, or shifts the footer downwards when a slow slot arrives.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when an empty slot leaves a hole or a late fill pushes the footer about. Answer no when the slot collapses cleanly and a late arrival lands in space already reserved.

criterion: A demonstration panel in the documentation column reaches the document around the panel, changing the page that hosts the panel.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a demonstration alters the page outside its own panel, navigates away, or writes to storage. Answer no when each demonstration stays sealed inside its own panel.

criterion: A demonstration in the documentation column runs past its time bound and takes the rest of the page down with the demonstration.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a runaway demonstration freezes the article beside the panel. Answer no when a demonstration over its bound is stopped and blanks its own panel alone.

criterion: A documentation page downloads the tour's three-dimensional engine before the article on the page is readable.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when opening a documentation page fetches the scene code or the editor computation. Answer no when each of the three front ends loads on its own route alone.
